newsitem.title: THAILAND: Crisis of confidence threatens Thai bank system.
newsitem.headline: Crisis of confidence threatens Thai bank system.

text.p: Central bank measures introduced to restore depositor confidence in Thailand's troubled finance system were vital to prevent further short-term instability in the troubled sector, analysts and executives said on Friday.
The Bank of Thailand moved to shore up confidence in the battered financial industry by pledging to guarantee depositors' and creditors' exposure to banks and finance companies.

The bank has also arranged to pump liquidity through the system by acting as a guarantor for interbank lending in what analysts said were increasingly desperate measures to plug holes in the banking system.

"I think there is a real crisis of confidence the Bank of Thailand has to deal with. By getting the foreign banks and the big banks to start extending liquidity into the system again is good news and it is vital and critical that happens," said one senior local bank analyst.
Pressure had been mounting on authorities to act following a run on deposits at some banks this week sparked by the closure of 42 ailing finance companies on Tuesday.
"When you get a run on deposits it's quite vital they stop it before you get a critical mass of people withdrawing their money," the analyst added.
Local bank executives said those runs, estimated to amount to billions of baht, are now easing but liquidity at the lower end of the banking sector remains tight.
Some banks have halted lending altogether to maintain liquidity, industry executives said.
Radio call-in shows have been inundated by nervous depositors seeking solace or advice, and at least one smaller bank has put piles of cash in public view to allay liquidity concerns.

While banks are reluctant to quantify levels of deposits and withdrawals this week, larger commercial banks are flush with cash as panicky depositors have sought safer repositories for their money, executives said.

"The trend overall has been for an increase in deposits and we have a surplus of deposits right now," said a member of the treasury department at Thai Farmers Bank Plc, the country's third largest commercial bank.
"It's good to have liquidity at the moment as no one knows where we go from here," said Pithi Sithi-Amnuai, executive vice-chairman at the country's largest lender Bangkok Bank Plc.
Though retail withdrawals are destabilising they are manageable providing cash is remitted somewhere within the domestic banking system, analysts said.

This is a key part of the central bank's deposit insurance scheme as it seeks to recycle cash deposited at the larger local banks and foreign banks onshore and feed liquidity throughout the whole system.

"If the money withdrawn is being deposited back elsewhere within the domestic system then the situation is manageable. The question is how much of the money withdrawn is being put back into the system," one senior bank analyst at a major European broker said.
With a bank holiday on Tuesday the market at least has a period of reflection in what promises to be a difficult week, analysts said.
"It is a very difficult time and I can see a number of problems upcoming. Next week we have to hope things settle down, there are not many avenues left," Pithi said.
